title.narrative: Improved basic services and increased livelihoods for and with media

description.narrative: Following the takeover by the de facto authorities in August 2021, the humanitarian, human rights, and economic situation in Afghanistan has sharply deteriorated over the past three years, reaching an unprecedented scale, with an estimated 23.7 million people in need of humanitarian assistance (out of a total population of 44.5 million). Human rights, especially those of women and girls, are severely curtailed, with restrictions on access to education, freedom of movement, freedom of expression and access to healthcare, to only name a few. Interventions by the international donor community focus on supporting the basic human needs and livelihoods of the people of Afghanistan, in which media play a critical role. At the same time, journalists can only play their critical role when they can exercise their profession as safely as possibly. This is particularly true for women journalists, around 80% of whom have lost their employment according to UNESCO-supported data. As such, the project will build on two key outcomes, with a “women-for-women”, human rights and do-not-harm based approach: 1) The Afghan population, particularly women, children and groups in vulnerable situations, including minorities, IDPs and returnees, have enhanced access to basic services via the media; 2) Resilient livelihoods are enhanced and job opportunities created for Afghan journalists and media workers, particularly women.
